title: Crawler corroboration is designed but unreachable, so one-vendor operators cannot corroborate at all
body:
Two corroboration paths exist in the design and neither can fire, and both matter more
than they look because each would corroborate a finding WITHOUT needing a second vendor.

1. THE `verified` RUNG IS NEVER SUPPLIED

`TriageInput.verifiedTicketIds` is documented as "ticket identities a non-opinionated
check has reproduced (crawler findings, a maintainer's repro). These promote straight to
`verified`." It is consumed in `triagePlaytestCorpus` (src/qa/triage.ts:197).

Nothing anywhere passes it. Not `bin/triage.ts`, not `loop.sh`, not any script — a
repo-wide search finds only the declaration and the read. So `verified`, the highest
promotion state and the only one that outranks corroboration, is unreachable by
construction. A live dev-loop exercise noticed the symptom without the cause: "I had no
reproduction to pass as verifiedTicketIds."

2. CRAWLER+FLEET AGREEMENT CANNOT OCCUR IN A QA TICKET

`rank.ts` calls it outright: "Crawler+fleet agreement on the same cluster is the
strongest signal", weighted `BOTH_SOURCES_BONUS = 2`. But `sessionIssueRecords` stamps
every issue `source: "fleet"` (src/qa/triage.ts:94), and `triagePlaytestCorpus` reads
only `input.sessions` — the playtest corpus. No crawler finding can enter a QA cluster,
so `hasBothSources` is false for every ticket the dev loop ever sees and the bonus is
dead code on this path.

WHY THIS IS WORTH MORE THAN IT LOOKS

Promotion today needs two model families or a reference-tier session. Both are LLM
opinions. The deterministic crawler is a different KIND of witness: no model, no persona,
a reproducible invariant violation. A crawler reproducing what a playtester complained
about is stronger evidence than two language models agreeing with each other, and it is
evidence a single-vendor operator can obtain today.

That is the practical sting. An operator with one vendor CLI — which is the common case,
since only Codex can currently run a live blind cohort — has no route to corroboration at
all, while the crawler that could provide one runs in the same repo on every cycle and
its findings are discarded before triage sees them.

THE WORK, ROUGHLY

The hard part is identity: a crawler finding names a location and an invariant, a ticket
is keyed on `cluster.key` over a location plus a token bag. Something has to decide that
a crawler softlock at `steading_yard` is the same finding as a playtester's complaint
there. Two shapes worth weighing:

  - Narrow: feed crawler findings into `sessionIssueRecords` as genuine `source:
    "crawler"` issues so they cluster by the existing machinery. Cheapest, reuses
    everything, and makes BOTH_SOURCES_BONUS live. Risk is that crawler prose is
    machine-generated and may not resemble a player's wording enough to cluster — worth
    measuring against the corpus before committing, exactly as the merge threshold was.
  - Explicit: compute `verifiedTicketIds` by matching crawler findings to existing
    tickets on canonical location plus invariant, and pass it from `bin/triage.ts`.
    More code, but it promotes to `verified` rather than merely adding weight, which is
    the documented intent.

Either way `bin/triage.ts` needs to read the crawler's output, which it does not today.

Worth deciding before building: the second matches what the field's docstring already
promises, so if that promise is meant, the explicit route is the honest one.

evidence.summary: verifiedTicketIds is never supplied by any caller, and crawler findings never enter QA triage, so both non-LLM corroboration paths are dead.
